subject: Minimum spend and graduated overage rate proposal
messages:
From: Julia Park <julia.park@greengrid.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@greengrid.com>
Date: Fri, 09 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Clarify minimum spend / overage for Hosted API

Hi Logan,

Thanks again for the product walkthrough yesterday. Legal and procurement asked me to confirm a couple of points before we escalate to procurement leadership:

1) Minimum monthly spend — our finance team wants to know if you require a hard minimum (e.g., $25k/mo) or if you offer a soft minimum with credits that roll forward.
2) Overage (on-demand) rate when we go above the committed monthly tokens — do you price bursts at the same on-demand rate as non-commit customers or do you offer a graduated overage schedule tied to the commit tier?
3) Burst caps / cushion — any way to buy a small burst cushion that only applies to short-term spikes without increasing the commit?

We want predictability but also the flexibility to handle seasonal spikes. Can you share a simple example with numbers (tokens -> $) so procurement can compare to other vendors?

Attachments: GreenGrid_MAAP_v1.pdf (the internal usage pattern they sent me)

Best,
Julia Park
Sr. Program Manager, GreenGrid
From: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
To: Julia Park <julia.park@greengrid.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 09 Jul 2027 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify minimum spend / overage for Hosted API

Julia — thanks for the clear list. I reviewed the MAAP and sketched two pragmatic options that balance predictability and flexibility. Attached is a one-page pricing grid and a worked example (proposed_pricing_grid.xlsx). High level:

Option A — Soft minimum + graduated overage (our recommended fit for GreenGrid)
- Minimum monthly commitment: $20,000 (credits applied to usage)
- Committed per-token rate: $0.00050/token (applies to committed volume)
- Graduated overage rates (on-demand above commit):
  - First 20% above commit: $0.00060/token
  - Next 50% above commit: $0.00065/token
  - >90% above commit: $0.00080/token (surcharge to discourage sustained overruns)
- Burst cushion: one-time purchase of 1.5x cushion credits equal to 10% of monthly commit. Cushion is consumed first during spikes and billed at first-tier overage ($0.00060). Unused cushion expires at month end.
- Quarterly true-up: we reconcile usage vs commit and roll forward unused commit credits one quarter (soft roll).

Example (month): committed $20k -> ≈40M tokens at $0.00050. If you hit 48M tokens (20% over), the extra 8M tokens billed at $0.00060. Total = committed $20k + overage 8M * $0.00060 = $4,800 -> $24,800.

Option B — Hard floor (organizational preference for cap + lower overage)
- Minimum monthly spend (hard): $30,000 (non-refundable floor)
- Committed per-token rate: $0.00045/token
- Overage flat rate (on-demand) above commit: $0.00075/token
- Burst cushion: included 5% of commit each month for free; sustained overages trigger automatic escalation to a dedicated capacity conversation.

Trade-offs: A keeps cash flexible and predictable but has slightly higher committed rate; B is better if you prefer the lowest committed unit cost and accept a hard floor.

Next steps: If you prefer Option A, we can add the graduated overage language into the exhibit and offer a 2-month free cushion on your first quarter to smooth initial spikes. If Option B, procurement will want the non-refundable floor spelled out and SLA credits adjusted.

Attachments: proposed_pricing_grid.xlsx

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick call with procurement to walk through the example.

—Logan
Logan Wright
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>, Julia Park <julia.park@greengrid.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Jul 2027 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify minimum spend / overage for Hosted API

Looping in a quick concession we can offer from pricing:

- For customers with clear seasonality like GreenGrid we can do a hybrid: $22k soft minimum with a 6-month ramp schedule. Ramp example: months 1-2 bill at 60% of commit, month 3 at 80%, month 4 onwards at full commit. This reduces upfront cash commitment.
- Replace the >90% surcharge with an upper-limit surcharge only if sustained overage persists for 2 consecutive months (gives you a safety net for one-off peaks).
- We can make the 10% burst cushion refundable as a credit if not used in the first quarter (one-time concession).

Operational ask for legal/procurement: please allow the following clause — quarterly true-up with a 30-day cure window to remediate incorrect usage flagging. If procurement wants stricter billing caps we can discuss a blended burst cap with an automatic fallback to a slightly higher committed rate.

I'll draft a short paragraph we can drop into the MSA. Logan — if you want me to, I'll prepare the MSA redline and pricing exhibit with the hybrid ramp.

Ben Carter
VP, Sales Operations, Redwood Inference
From: Julia Park <julia.park@greengrid.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@greengrid.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Jul 2027 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify minimum spend / overage for Hosted API

Logan / Ben — this is very helpful, thank you. GreenGrid preference is Option A with the hybrid ramp Ben proposed (soft minimum $22k with the 6-month ramp) and the refundable cushion concession for quarter one. Procurement will still want the >90% surcharge to require a two-month sustained trigger (we agree to that).

Please send a redline exhibit and a one-page summary we can attach to our procurement submission. If you can include the worked example for our typical month (MAAP attached) that will move this to our sourcing committee next week.

Next steps: Logan — can you send the redline + short summary by EOD Wednesday (2027-07-14)? Julia will route to sourcing.

Thanks,
Julia Park
Sr. Program Manager, GreenGrid
